chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Humran from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'If a person in ihram intentionally kills a bird between As-Safa and Al-Marwah,' he said: 'He must pay fidyah and compensation, and he will be flogged.' I said: 'If he kills it in the Ka'bah intentionally,' he said: 'He must pay fidyah and compensation, he will be flogged less than the full hadd penalty, and he will be turned around for the people so that others may take heed.'

key_terms.الْجَزَاءُ: Compensation or retribution, often referring to the value of the killed item
key_terms.دُونَ الْحَدِّ: Less than the fixed hadd penalty
key_terms.فِدَاءٌ: Fidyah, a compensation or ransom paid for breaking a ritual restriction
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يَنْكُلَ: To take heed or be cautious
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: He will be subjected to ta'zir (discretionary punishment/flogging)
key_terms.يُقْلَبُ: He will be turned around (displayed to the people)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in ihram who intentionally kills a bird?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), distinguishing the penal consequences for a pilgrim who intentionally kills a bird based on location: between Safa and Marwah, the offender faces fidyah, compensation, and ta'zir (discretionary punishment), whereas killing within the Ka'bah precincts warrants a lighter flogging (duna al-hadd) and public humiliation (iqalab) to serve as a deterrent. This highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where the sanctity of the specific location influences the severity and nature of the corporal punishment applied to the offender.
